lastPrompt: This is an operating-systems course lab (Projects 1–6) that implements a RISC-V bare-metal operating system. The repo spans six incremental projects: a bootloader, a simple cooperative kernel, a preemptive kernel with SMP, an interactive OS with process management and IPC, a virtual-memory-enabled kernel with demand paging, a device-driver layer with network support, and a file system. Entire subsystems have been removed and must be re-implemented. Your working directory is `/workspace`. The project code is already present in seven subdirectories: `Project1-Bootloader`, `Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part1`, `Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part2`, `[redacted]`, `Project4-Virtual_Memory_Management`, `Project5-Device_Driver`, and `Project6-File_System`. Implement the following modules: The following modules need to be implemented or substantially built out. All stubbed function bodies contain `/* TODO: implement */`. Bootloader Image Builder (`Project1-Bootloader/createimage.c`): The host-side tool that reads ELF binaries and writes a bootable disk image. Two functions handle segment writing and OS size recording. (~1 file, 2 functions to implement) Part 1 Scheduler & Locking (`[redacted].c`, `kernel/locking/lock.c`): The cooperative round-robin scheduler, task blocking/unblocking primitives, and mutex lock acquire/release. (~2 files, 5 functions to implement) Part 2 Scheduler & Synchronisation (`Project2-A_Simple_Kernel_Part2/kernel/`): The preemptive priority-based scheduler with ready-queue management, priority-based task selection, timer expiration checking, mutex locking, binary semaphore operations, and futex wait/wakeup with hash-based node management. (~5 files, 9 functions to implement) Process Management & IPC (`[redacted]/`): Multi-core scheduler with process lifecycle management (spawn, exit, kill, waitpid), priority-based scheduling with CPU affinity masks, binary semaphore tracking, and a mailbox-based inter-process communication system for sending and receiving messages with blocking semantics. (~4 files, 12 functions to implement) Virtual Memory Management (`[redacted].c`, `kernel/sched/sched.c`): SV39 three-level page table initialisation and teardown, user page allocation with NRU page replacement, swap-to-disk eviction, demand-paging page fault handling, shared memory mapping/unmapping, process creation/execution with ELF loading, and process termination with resource cleanup. (~2 files, 13 functions to implement) Device Driver Layer (`Project5-Device_Driver/drivers/net.c`, `kernel/mm/mm.c`, `kernel/sched/sched.c`): Network packet send/receive with poll and interrupt modes, IRQ mode switching, plus the full virtual memory and scheduler subsystems carried forward from Project 4 with additional page-helper functionality. (~3 files, 18 functions to implement) File System (`Project6-File_System/kernel/fs/`): A complete on-disk file system with superblock/bitmap-based allocation, inode and block management (alloc, free), directory operations (mkdir, rmdir, ls, cd), hard/soft linking, file operations (touch, cat, fopen, fread, fwrite), plus the full scheduler and virtual memory subsystems from Project 5. (~6 files, 24 functions to implement) The tests also depend on these signatures and entry points: The following functions are called or inspected directly by the test suite. You must implement them with these exact signatures: `static void write_segment(Elf64_Phdr phdr, FILE *fp, FILE *img, int *nbytes)` — writes an ELF segment to a disk image with 512-byte alignment `static void write_os_size(int nbytes, FILE *img)` — writes the OS sector count at offset 508 in the image `void do_scheduler(void)` (P2A) — cooperative round-robin scheduler `void do_block(list_node_t *pcb_node, list_head *queue)` (P2A) — moves a PCB to a block queue `void do_unblock(list_node_t *pcb_node)` (P2A) — moves a PCB back to the ready queue `void do_mutex_lock_acquire(mutex_lock_t *lock)` (P2A, P2B) — acquires a mutex with blocking `void do_mutex_lock_r
